newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH '98 BUDGET GAP LIKELY LOWER THAN IN '97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH '98 BUDGET GAP LIKELY LOWER THAN IN '97.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka on Wednesday said that next year's budget deficit would be difficult to finance if it remained at the 1997 planned level of 2.8 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP).
"We believe that it is unlikely that a deficit comparable to this year's would be possible to finance (in 1998)," Belka told a news conference.

Late on Tuesday the central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the finance ministry was working on a 1998 budget draft which envisioned a budget deficit of only 1.8 percent of GDP, but Belka said the gap may be higher than that.
"I don't know whether the budget deficit will be on the scale as the central bank president said, but we are certanily going in that direction," Belka said.
He also said the finance ministry was having serious difficulties in placing paper on markets.
"We are having serious problems placing various papers on the market," Belka said without elaborating.
Yields on most Polish debt instruments grew for the first four months of this year before dipping over the last month.
